name: Seror
title: Ancestor of King Saul
summary: Seror was a man from the tribe of Benjamin and an ancestor of Israel's first king, Saul. He is mentioned in the genealogy as the father of Abiel and the grandfather of Kish, who was Saul's father. His significance lies in his place in the genealogical line that led to Israel's first kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Saul's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Seror is mentioned as part of King Saul's lineage when Saul's father Kish is introduced in the narrative. He is the son of Bekorat and the father of Abiel.

keyEvents.title: Saul's Genealogy and Royal Lineage
keyEvents.description: Through the lineage Seror – Abiel – Kish – Saul, the tribe of Benjamin became the tribe that gave Israel its first king.

keyEvents.title: Kish Searches for the Donkeys
keyEvents.description: Saul's father Kish, who was a descendant of Zeruor, sent his son Saul out to look for lost donkeys, which led to Saul's meeting with the prophet Samuel.

keyEvents.title: Saul Anointed as King
keyEvents.description: As part of God's plan, Saul, a descendant of Zeruor, was anointed by the prophet Samuel to become Israel's first king.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Tribe of Benjamin in Israel's History
keyEvents.description: Zeruor belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, one of the smallest tribes in Israel, yet it was the tribe chosen to provide the nation with its first king.
